issues.description: code_style §2 requires package_type to be declared correctly (tool = "application"), but the CLI-tool recipe omits package_type entirely (0 occurrences). Non-blocking: preflight PF8's CLI detection uses non-empty cpp_info.bindirs, which IS set (bindirs = ["bin"]), and the aligned software-level commands.json exists, so no gate fails. Style deviation only.
issues.fix_suggestion: Add `package_type = "application"` to the Jtreg7Conan class attributes (after `settings`).

issues.description: code_style §1 requires conanfile.py files to start with shebang + docstring naming the software; the main recipe complies, but test_package/conanfile.py starts directly with `from conan import ConanFile` (same deviation exists in the sibling jtreg6/jtreg8 packages). Non-blocking style item.
issues.fix_suggestion: Prepend `#!/usr/bin/env python3` and a one-line docstring, e.g. """Conan test_package - jtreg7 7.5.2-1 (GNU make)."""

issues.description: code_style §16 import order: third-party import (`from conan import ConanFile`) precedes the stdlib import (`import os`) with no blank-line group separation. The main recipe orders imports correctly (stdlib block, blank line, conan block). Non-blocking style item.
issues.fix_suggestion:
Reorder to:
import os

from conan import ConanFile

issues.description: Bootstrap failure-path robustness (happy path unaffected; mirrors the P3 recorded for sibling jtreg8): if an earlier interrupted bootstrap left a partial ~/bishengjdk17 without bin/java, os.rename(root, target) fails on the existing directory and the re-raised OSError aborts the build without clearing the stale partial install; an exception inside tarfile.extractall (lines 144-148) leaks the staging dir and the ~286MB tarball because cleanup is only on handled paths (no try/finally).
issues.fix_suggestion: On rename OSError with a target lacking bin/java, rmtree(target) then retry the rename once; wrap the extract/publish block in try/finally to always rmtree(staging) and best-effort remove the tarball.

issues.description: _fetch's python-urllib fallback builds ssl._create_unverified_context(), disabling TLS certificate verification for the Ant / TestNG-LICENSE / JDK-fallback downloads. Acceptable in practice because every _fetch result is hash-verified after download (sha1 for Ant and TestNG LICENSE, sha256 for the JDK), so tampering is detected; noted for consistency with the sibling audit.
issues.fix_suggestion: Attempt a default verifying SSL context first and fall back to the unverified context only on certificate failure, keeping the existing post-download hash checks.

summary: W4 pre-PR audit of jtreg7/7.5.2-1 (10 changed files, all under archives/j/jtreg7/, single-package PR, W2 satisfied). VERDICT PASS: zero P0/P1; only non-blocking P2 style deviations and P3 robustness suggestions. Adversarial verification performed: (1) sha256 independently reproduced against the official source: downloading https://github.com/openjdk/jtreg/archive/refs/tags/jtreg-7.5.2+1.tar.gz (608,665 bytes) yields ce0c9971f951dffa4b3b85044ffe76a97d5ad9e0f5d6d0e218ceee2ce60df341, byte-identical to conandata.yml and manifest.yaml; URL is the official OpenJDK GitHub tag, HTTPS, no file:// or mirror/ghfast leftovers in conandata (pf7/R39 clean). (2) The single patch 0001-make-Platform.gmk.patch applies cleanly (git apply rc=0, reverse-check rc=0) to the real upstream make/Platform.gmk and adds a substantive HarmonyOS->linux branch (OS_NAME/OS_ARCH/OS_VERSION, same semantics as the Linux branch) with zero platform macros or -D injection (R8/R3 clean); no prebuilt binaries anywhere (R19 clean). (3) test_package is a genuine consumer test: it runs the PACKAGED bin/jtreg (a shell entry generated by jtreg.gmk) and bin/jtdiff against a mini JDK suite with 1 passing + 1 intentionally failing test as negative control, asserting exit code, aggregate 'passed: 1; failed: 1', summary.txt lines and .jtr contents; exactly 12 ok() assertions == MANIFEST.yml assertion_count 12 (R34/R9 clean, not an empty or skipped test). (4) R38/PF8: software-level commands.json declares name=jtreg7, type=tool, versions[7.5.2-1].ref=jtreg7/7.5.2-1, aligned with the recipe name/version and version directory; settings four fields present; validate() matches os in (Linux, OHOS) (R32), no hardcoded compiler/toolchain env (R33), Conan 2 API only. (5) R51: MANIFEST's upstream_check_command is byte-identical to the upstream CI workflow (.github/workflows/test.yml verified byte-identical to the tarball) and the recipe actually executes it in build() (MAKE_ARGS=quick-test HEADLESS=1 ... --skip-download); the quick-test target resolves to checkJavaOSVersion + BUILDTESTDIR + 8 INITIAL_TESTS = 10, matching the declared 'All (10) selected tests completed successfully'; full-suite 257/253/4 results are disclosed with per-test root causes, no placeholders/TBD/待验证 text in any changed file. (6) Hygiene: all changed files are LF-only and BOM-free, no TODO/FIXME/XXX/print()/secrets/tokens; conanfile.py + test_package/conanfile.py compile under Python 3.10 (py_compile rc=0); conandata/manifest sha256 format is 64-hex and equal. Judgment notes (no invented violations): R26 static-link rule is inapplicable (pure Java tool, no .so/.a); R40 deep-adaptation domains (graphics/UI/multimedia/peripherals) do not apply, and the adaptation is a real platform-detection fix exercised end-to-end by the consumer test; settings compiler/build_type are not consumed by the Java build by design (documented in-recipe, kept for L0p); the two software-level files (README.md, commands.json) are required by the archive spec and are the documented PF9 false positive, not a violation; test.sh's /storage/Users/currentUser JDK fallback paths are device-home expansions behind $HOME/JAVA_HOME precedence (no secrets, no source-URL absolute paths); PR body itself (reports/pr-body.md) is not part of the audit input, but no placeholder residue exists in any changed file. The remaining findings are style-only (P2) and robustness suggestions (P3), which do not block PR creation.
